355625.title: Rota–Mason conjectures on unimodality and log-concavity of Whitney numbers
355625.literal_statement:
Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a loopless matroid of rank $k$ and cardinality $n$, and let $W_i$ be the number of flats of rank $i$. **Whitney-number coefficient conjectures.** The sequence $W_0,\ldots,W_k$ is unimodal, the sequence $W_0,\ldots,W_k$ is log-concave with $W_i^2\geq W_{i-1}W_{i+1}$ for $1\leq i\leq k-1$, and the normalized sequence $W_0/\binom n0,\ldots,W_k/\binom nk$ is log-concave, equivalently

$$
W_i^2\geq\frac{i+1}{i}\frac{n-i+1}{n-i}W_{i-1}W_{i+1}\qquad(1\leq i\leq k-1).
$$

These are the classical coefficient conjectures for the $\mathrm{W}$-polynomial, attributed in the paper to Rota and Mason. The source says that the unimodality conjecture remains open; no resolution status is supplied for the full combined list.

355716.title: The word-map nonconstancy conjecture for simple compact Lie groups
355716.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected simple compact Lie group with trivial center. A **non-constant word** is an element of $G\ast F_d$ that does not lie in $G$ itself; its evaluation on $G^d$ is the associated word map.

**Word-map nonconstancy conjecture.** Every non-constant word defines a non-constant word map.

The trivial-center hypothesis is necessary, since a nontrivial central element produces a non-constant word with constant evaluation. The claim also fails for certain semisimple, non-simple compact groups, while the conjecture asks for the corresponding nonconstancy property in the simple case.
355716.assessment: Requires arbitrary reduced words with coefficients in connected centerless compact simple Lie groups; coefficient-free word theorems and central/semisimple counterexamples do not meet the hypotheses. No all-word mechanism.

355750.title: Coloring probability inequality for minimal elements of posets
355750.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a connected $n$-element poset with minimal elements $m_1,\ldots,m_s$. Define a coloring $c:P\to\mathcal{P}([s])$ by putting $i\in c(x)$ if $x\geq_P m_i$, where $[s]=\{1,\ldots,s\}$. Let $L_{n-2}$ denote the labeling obtained after $n-2$ applications of promotion, and let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the relevant probability distribution on labelings.

**Coloring probability conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{P}\left(c(L_{n-2}^{-1}(1))=\{s\}\,\middle|\,L(m_{s-1})=n\right)\geq\mathbb{P}\left(c(L_{n-2}^{-1}(1))=\{s\}\,\middle|\,L(m_s)=n\right).
$$

The paper states that this inequality would imply the general bound for tangled labelings by showing that the number of tangled labelings increases when $m_{s-1}\lessdot m_s$; it remains open.
355750.assessment: Need source uniform-labeling probability space, s>=2 conditioning and a promotion-compatible injection preserving the final colour event. Swapping the labels on two minima need not preserve promotion trajectories. Malformed s=1 domain is correction only.

355767.title: The disconnected contact-poset conjecture
355767.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a disconnected poset. A poset is **Frobenius** when its associated type-A Lie poset algebra has index zero, and it is **toral** when it has the toral construction form described in the paper. The disjoint sum of two posets is their union with no comparabilities between the two components.

**Disconnected contact-poset conjecture.** $\mathcal{P}$ is contact if and only if it is a disjoint sum of two Frobenius, toral posets.

The paper explains that this conjecture would follow from the toral-poset conjecture for Frobenius posets, together with known results on disconnected contact type-A Lie poset algebras. The source gives no resolution status.

355806.title: Thomas–Williams' rowmotion order conjecture for rational Tamari lattices
355806.literal_statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be relatively prime positive integers. Let $\operatorname{Tam}(a,b)$ be the rational Tamari lattice of lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(a,b)$ lying strictly above $y=(b/a)x$ except at their endpoints, and let $\operatorname{Row}$ denote its rowmotion operator.

**Thomas–Williams' conjecture.** The operator

$$
\operatorname{Row}\colon\operatorname{Tam}(a,b)\to\operatorname{Tam}(a,b)
$$

has order $a+b-1$.

This conjecture gives the period of rowmotion on every rational Tamari lattice. The paper proves it for the subfamily of $m$-Tamari lattices, while the general case remains open.
355806.assessment: m-Tamari subfamily does not prove arbitrary coprime(a,b). Exact order versus period needs both upper bound and an orbit/lcm lower bound. a=1 singleton gives literal endpoint issue only, not significant discovery.

355860.title: Smith normal form conjecture for the walk matrix of the extended Dynkin graph
355860.literal_statement:
Let $\tilde{D}_n$ be the extended Dynkin graph with $n+1$ vertices, let $W(\tilde{D}_n)$ be its walk matrix, and set

$$
r=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

**Smith normal form conjecture.** The Smith normal form of $W(\tilde{D}_n)$ is

$$
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{diag}(\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{r-1},n-1,0,\ldots,0), & \text{if $n$ is even},\\
\operatorname{diag}\left(\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{r-1},\frac{n-1}{2},0,\ldots,0\right), & \text{if $n$ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture gives the remaining Smith normal form data after the paper determines the rank of the walk matrix, and its verification would complete the proposed next step for the extended Dynkin graphs $\tilde{D}_n$.

356664.literal_statement: Let a Costas sequence be a sequence whose difference triangle has no repeated entry in any row. 356673.title: Directed forcing conjecture for oriented graphs
356673.literal_statement: Let $B$ be an oriented graph, let $\overline{B}$ be its underlying undirected graph obtained by forgetting edge directions, and call $B$ directed-forcing when it has the directed forcing property. **Directed forcing conjecture.** If $B$ has a homomorphism to an edge and $\overline{B}$ contains a cycle, then $B$ has the directed forcing property. The paper proves that a homomorphism to an edge and a cycle in the underlying graph are necessary conditions for directed forcing. It conjectures that these two conditions are also sufficient, leaving the characterization open.
356673.assessment: Homomorphism to a directed edge means all arcs go across bipartition in one direction, but a cycle alone does not prove the universal quasirandomness forcing property. Need full density-equality-to-quasirandomness mechanism; flagship-type structural conjecture parked.

356691.title: The pairwise-adjacent vertices-or-edges conjecture for triangle-free graphs
356691.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an $coverline{K_3}$-free graph on $n$ vertices. A set of vertices or edges is **pairwise adjacent** when every two members are adjacent, where adjacency between an edge and another member has the natural incidence/endpoint interpretation used in the source.

**Pairwise-adjacent vertices-or-edges conjecture.** Every $coverline{K_3}$-free graph on $n$ vertices has a set of

$$
\left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil
$$

pairwise adjacent vertices or edges.

This conjecture is presented as an obstacle to reconciling two algorithmic approaches for proving restricted forms of Hadwiger's Conjecture. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
